dreams.pitch: Your own dungeon crawler for the terminal: a hero you design, a maze carved by recursion, goblins, dragons, a shop that gives change, save codes and a high score table. Every lesson writes the next piece, and by the end you play a game made entirely of your own code.
dreams.summary: A seeded, turn-based dungeon crawler (C# console), assembled from your passing code.
features: A title screen and a hero whose stats you choose (lesson 1)
Fights with armour, levels and a combat log that prints its own trace table
A map drawn with nested loops, with fog that lifts as you explore
A new maze on every floor, carved by your recursive backtracker from a seed
Locked stairs, dragon floors on the prime numbers, a shop that gives change in gold, silver and copper
Retro save codes in base 32, a high score board, and the game's own tests: `dotnet run -- check`

out: Five floors down. One way out.
=== Floor 2 of 5 ===   A dragon (D) guards the key on this floor.
The dragon drops a key. The seal on the stairs breaks.

README.md: # Delve
A seeded, turn-based dungeon crawler for the terminal, written by you in the code-dojo
**Programming fundamentals** track. Every lesson replaces one stub in `src/` with your own passing code.
```text
dotnet run            play the dungeon from seed 7
dotnet run -- 42      a different dungeon: any number is a seed
dotnet run -- check   run the checks you wrote (tests/DelveChecks.cs) against your pieces
Commands in the game: `n s e w` move, `i` inventory, `p` drink a potion, `r` rotate your belt
(sword: +2 attack, shield: +2 armour, lantern: see further), `buy` a potion, `save` prints a save code,
`look`, `help`, `q` quits. Reach the stairs `>` on each of the five floors: find the key `k`, and on
dragon floors (the prime-numbered ones) defeat the dragon `D` for it.
| File | Piece | Built in |
| `src/Banner.cs` | the title screen | State and values: Named boxes |
| `src/Hero.cs` | your hero's stats, `RotateSlots` | State and values: Named boxes |
| `src/Damage.cs` | `Damage`, `Level`, `XpToNext` | State and values: Whole numbers and fractions |
| `src/Stats.cs` | `Heal` (overflow-proof), `Percent` | State and values: Where numbers break |
| `src/Shop.cs` | `ToCopper`, `Coins`, `Change` | State and values: Boss |
| `src/Rules.cs` | `CanOpenDoor`, `IsMonster`, `IsItem` | Logic: Truth tables |
| `src/Bounds.cs` | `IsOutsideMap`, `IsWall` | Logic: De Morgan and short-circuits |
| `src/Moves.cs` | `MoveOutcome` | Logic: Clear conditions |
| `src/Encounter.cs` | what each dead end holds | Logic: Boss |
| `src/Inventory.cs` | `TotalWeight`, `IndexOfMax` | Loops: Counting and accumulating |
| `src/GameLoop.cs` | the loop that reads your commands | Loops: Edges and endings |
| `src/Map.cs` | `Render`: the map with fog | Loops: Loops inside loops |
| `src/Floors.cs` | dragon floors are the prime floors | Loops: Boss |
| `src/Hud.cs` | the status line | Functions and recursion: Breaking work into functions |
| `src/Depth.cs` | the climb back up, recursively | Functions and recursion: Scope and the call stack |
| `src/Maze.cs` | `Carve`: the recursive maze | Functions and recursion: Recursion |
| `src/MazeReach.cs` | `CountReachable`: flood fill | Functions and recursion: Recursion or a loop? |
| `src/SaveCode.cs` | base-32 save codes | Functions and recursion: Boss |
| `src/CombatLog.cs` | `Fight` prints its own trace table | Thinking like a programmer: Tracing by hand |
| `src/Scores.cs` | the high score board | Thinking like a programmer: Breaking problems down |
| `tests/DelveChecks.cs` | the game's own tests | Thinking like a programmer: Edge cases and testing |
| `src/Loot.cs` | chest values, average loot (debugged) | Thinking like a programmer: Debugging on purpose |
| `src/Reveal.cs` | the spiral map reveal | Thinking like a programmer: Boss |
| `src/Play.cs` | the whole game, wired by you | Thinking like a programmer: Boss (Ship Delve) |
`src/Engine.cs` is the part you did not write: game state, turns, fights, the shop and the score
file (`%USERPROFILE%\.delve\scores.txt`, or the folder in `DELVE_HOME`). Every piece is a `static`
function in the one `partial class Game`, so pieces can call each other; keep helper names unique.
